speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning. I understand you are experiencing shortness of breath and notice your abdomen has swollen significantly. Can you describe when these symptoms first started and if you have any pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any pain or discomfort in your abdomen, and have you noticed any changes in your menstrual cycle or bowel habits? REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal Ultrasound: Large mass in the right ovary, significant ascites present.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a family history of ovarian or breast cancer, and have you experienced any recent weight loss or fatigue? REQUEST TEST: CA-125

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of gastrointestinal issues or unexplained weight loss, and are you experiencing early satiety or difficulty breathing when lying flat? REQUEST TEST: CT_Abdomen_Pelvis

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the large ovarian mass and ascites with a normal CA-125 and unremarkable CT, this presentation is highly suggestive of Meigs syndrome. I will examine the patient for signs of a fibroma and check for resolution of symptoms upon potential surgical removal. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Shortness of breath. I also have Increased abdominal girth, Fatigue, No significant weight loss or gain.

speaker: Doctor
text: The triad of ovarian fibroma, ascites, and pleural effusion causing your shortness of breath confirms the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Meigs Syndrome
